sections.html:
Part of Longmont lies in northeastern Boulder County and a smaller part reaches into western Weld County. Check which one holds your parcel before anything else. It decides who sends your tax bill and which clerk files your deed.

The 2020 census recorded 98,885 people and 41,680 housing units, with 4.8 percent vacant. Vacancy among owner-occupied homes was only 0.9 percent, so houses rarely stay empty for long. Because population doubled in the 1960s and again in the 1970s, the housing stock mixes several eras. A block off Main Street and a subdivision near the interstate can feel like different cities, so price talk begins with the address.

Buyers range from school and hospital staff to tech and aerospace workers and commuters bound for Boulder or Denver. A new job in the household often forces a Longmont owner to sell against a deadline.

Owners choose between halves and a single payment. Paying early earns no discount. Interest on a late first half starts at 1 percent in March and reaches 6 percent by August, while second-half and full payments follow their own schedule. After September, ask the treasurer for exact amounts.

The Longmont branch is at 515 Coffman Street, Suite 113. It keeps limited hours, with Monday as the open day, so call before you drive over.

sections.h2: Weld County parcels and the deed fee
sections.html: A parcel in the Weld County portion means dealing with Weld County for taxes and recording. State law adds a documentary fee of 1 cent for each $100 on transfers above $500, and each deed lists the buyer's mailing address, which is where later tax statements are sent. Negotiate in the contract who bears the fee.

Anyone renting for stays under 30 days, whether a whole dwelling or rooms in an owner-occupied home, needs a city license that renews yearly. A sales and use tax license is part of the requirement. Existing rentals get no exemption, and unlicensed operators face code enforcement.

Applicants must be Longmont residents. File through the city's Accela Citizen Access system or visit the Development Services Center at 385 Kimbark Street. Code enforcement takes questions at (303) 651-8695.

Did the house ever appear on Airbnb, VRBO or a similar site? Verify the license history before you sign a purchase contract. A gap in licensing raises questions for ordinary buyers and for investors who underwrite rental income.

Longmont swings from hot summers to hard winters, and that range punishes roofs, furnaces and air conditioners. An inspector hired by a conventional buyer will check all three. A tired roof or a failing heater is where many financed sales stall. With deferred maintenance on the house, obtain repair estimates first, then weigh a repaired listing against an as-is sale.

sections.h2: Questions to settle before a cash offer
sections.html:
The answers below decide how fast a sale can close.

  • Boulder or Weld: which county holds the parcel, and are current taxes paid?
  • Has the home ever run as a short-term rental, and did it carry a license?
  • Who lives in the house, and what does the lease say?
  • Are any permits open, liens attached or utility balances unpaid?
  • How old are the roof, furnace and cooling equipment? A buyer prices those first.

We look at Longmont houses in almost any condition. If you are weighing a cash sale against a listing, give us the address and your situation, and we will lay out how each path would play out for that property.

After you say yes, a title company takes the lead. It checks ownership, hunts for liens, orders the tax certificate from the correct county and drafts the deed. You sign, the county clerk files the deed, and your proceeds arrive once taxes and any mortgage are paid off. No lender appraisal sits in the way, so the closing date tracks the title work and your move.

Occupied houses need one more step. For a tenant-occupied house, the buyer wants the lease and a sense of whether the tenant will stay. If you live there yourself, line up your move-out with the closing so the keys change hands when the money does.

Bring a photo ID to the signing, plus anything the title company requested in advance, such as a payoff letter from your lender or paperwork showing who may sign for an estate.

Heirs, tired landlords, owners untangling an unlicensed rental past, and anyone whose repair list outruns their budget often like the as-is route. A house in good shape with an owner in no rush may do better on the open market, and requesting an offer first costs nothing. Place the number beside a realistic listing outcome and pick the trade-off you can live with.

Retail buyers usually hire an inspector, and the report becomes a repair list. Common Longmont items include roof age, furnace condition and cooling capacity. Walk your own house with that eye before you decide. Note which items you could fix cheaply and which are costly. A cash buyer sees the same list and prices it once, which is why many sellers find the as-is number easier to read than a long negotiation after a report. It also spares you the awkward moment of a lender-driven repair request arriving a week before closing, when you have already packed boxes.

Where the calendar lands affects the closing statement. A sale in the weeks around the second-half date means the title company will check whether that installment is paid or still open. A sale after the full-payment deadline in April means the first half has already been settled or has begun to accrue interest. Ask the treasurer's office what shows on the parcel, hand the answer to the title company and avoid guessing. Surprises on a closing statement are almost always tax or lien items that someone assumed were paid.

Whether it is a long-term tenant or a former short-term unit, a rental brings paperwork. Gather the lease, the rent history and, for short-term use, the license and tax filings. A buyer who plans to continue the rental will ask for them. A buyer who wants a vacant house will ask when the tenant leaves. Giving both answers up front keeps the offer from changing late in the process.

faqs.q: Is Longmont in Boulder County or Weld County?
faqs.a: Both. Most of Longmont is in Boulder County, and the city stretches east into western Weld County. The county holding your parcel sends the tax bill and records your deed.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Boulder County?
faqs.a: Half payments fall at the end of February and on June 15, and a single full payment is due April 30. A weekend pushes the February date to the next business day.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Longmont house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. Rentals under 30 days require an annual city license plus a sales and use tax license, and only Longmont residents can apply.

faqs.q: What is the state documentary fee on a Colorado home sale?
faqs.a: One cent per $100 of consideration on a transfer above $500. Your closing agent can confirm the exact amount.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Longmont house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Many owners sell as-is, and a cash buyer prices the repairs into the offer. Compare that against the cost and time of fixing the house first.
